_comment: PURPOSE: make the imports resolve. Nothing else.
Every pipeline script imports its siblings by BARE NAME (`engine`, `models_panel`,
`or_key`, `provider_lock`, ...) and gets away with it because `common/_paths.py` inserts
the stage folders into sys.path at import time. That works at runtime and is invisible to
static analysis, so without the extraPaths below Pylance flags every one of those imports
as unresolved -- a wall of false warnings that hides the real ones.
typeCheckingMode is OFF, and deliberately so. Merely creating this file makes Pyright use
its own default mode ('standard') instead of the editor's, which on a codebase with no type
annotations produces a second wall of false positives: `arg('--workers', 24, int)` looks
wrong because arg()'s `cast` parameter defaults to str; `MAX_TOKENS[ARM]` looks wrong
because arg() can return None, even though the line above it raises SystemExit unless ARM
is 'on' or 'off'; post() looks like it can return None because Pyright cannot prove the
retry loop's last iteration always returns. Trading one wall of noise for another is not a
fix. If this repo ever adopts annotations, raise this to 'basic' and work through the real
Keep extraPaths in sync with the list common/_paths.py inserts.
